terms.meaning: The extremely small particles that all matter is made of.
The gap between the particles of a substance.
The force that holds the particles together.
The lowest temperature at which a solid melts into a liquid at atmospheric pressure.
A liquid or gas: anything that can flow.
Particles of liquids and gases keep moving, so one substance spreads through another.

items.name: Particles in a solid
items.formula: Closely packed with the strongest attraction. They only vibrate in place.
items.example: A solid has a fixed shape and volume, and it is hard to compress.

items.name: Particles in a liquid
items.formula: Attraction is a little weaker, so particles move within a limited space.
items.example: A liquid has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container.

items.name: Particles in a gas
items.formula: Attraction is negligible and the spaces are the largest, so particles move freely.
items.example: A gas has no fixed shape or volume, and it can be compressed easily.

items.name: Syringe test
items.formula: With the nozzle closed, air can be pushed in but water cannot.
items.example: This shows that gas particles have much more space between them.

items.name: Melting points
items.example: Iron’s particles are held much more strongly than those of ice.

items.name: Evaporation and boiling
items.formula: Evaporation is slow, from the surface, at all temperatures. Boiling happens at the boiling point.
items.example: Wet clothes dry without being boiled.

items.name: Sugar in water
items.formula: The level barely rises, because sugar particles go into the spaces between water particles.
items.example: The sugar seems to disappear, but the water tastes sweet.

items.name: Potassium permanganate in water
items.formula: One grain slowly colours all the water, because the particles keep moving.
items.example: It spreads faster in hot water.

items.name: Smell across a room
items.formula: Perfume particles mix with moving air and spread in all directions.
items.example: An incense stick lit in a corner soon fills the room.

items.name: Grinding chalk
items.formula: It only makes smaller grains, each still holding many particles of chalk.

items.name: Acharya Kanad
items.formula: Taught long ago that matter is made of tiny particles called parmanu.
items.example: He wrote about this in the Vaisheshika Sutras.

items.name: How soap cleans
items.formula: One end of a soap particle holds oil and the other end holds water.
items.example: The oil is lifted off the cloth in the wash.

mistakes.text: Attraction is strongest in solids and weakest in gases, not the other way round.
Particles in a solid are not completely still. They vibrate about fixed positions.
Dust and soot specks are not single particles of matter. Each holds a huge number of them.
